newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: German President commemorates Irish refugee aid.
newsitem.headline: German President commemorates Irish refugee aid.

text.p: German president Roman Herzog paid a one-day visit to Ireland on Sunday to mark the 50th anniversary of "Operation Shamrock" when Irish families opened their homes to children from stricken post-war Germany.

Herzog called on Irish President Mary Robinson at her official residence before the two attended a Dublin church service to commemorate the humanitarian response of families who fostered more than 500 young refugees during 1946-47.
Many of the original foster children travelled from Germany and were set for a nostalgic meeting with host families.

Officials said up to 160 former refugees and 180 foster families had accepted invitations from the Irish Red Cross Society and the German Embassy to ceremonies including a service at the capital's St Patrick's Cathedral and a reception in historic Dubin Castle.
Families struck by reports of misery and hunger affecting children gave the youngsters temporary homes in an initiative named after Ireland's national emblem.
Another 500 children from Britain, France and elsewhere were also fostered in Ireland under "Operation Shamrock".
The Germans, mostly from the Rhineland area, stayed for three years or more. Religious organisations and the Red Cross co-operated in arranging their arrival.
On Monday the "foster children" and families will visit a hostel in Glencree County Wicklow, near Dublin, where the young ones stayed before joining their hosts.
Deputy prime minister and foreign minister Dick Spring will later hold a reception for them at his ministerial headquarters in the Irish capital.
